title: When life is at risk, donor blood is not always there.
intro: Across the living world, extraordinary species face unique challenges. Even with the best care, access to donor blood can be limited, precisely when it is needed most.

image.alt: Endangered Sumatran tiger walking through a green habitat, representing wildlife diversity and species protection
image.credit: Joe Milmoe, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

cards.title: Species diversity
cards.text: Stronger species help safeguard both nature and people.

image.alt: African forest elephant family at a remote forest water source, representing wildlife-care logistics
image.credit: Daphne Carlson Bremer, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

cards.title: Operational reality
cards.text: In remote areas, donor supply, storage, and logistics can be limited or unavailable.

image.alt: Critically endangered hawksbill sea turtle swimming above a coral reef, representing remote conservation-care needs
image.credit: GP Schmahl, NOAA Flower Garden Banks National Marine Sanctuary

cards.title: Oxygen-delivery gap
cards.text: Oxygen-delivery options may bridge critical needs when donor blood is unavailable or delayed.

quoteLines: Across species. Across continents. A shared need. A stronger tomorrow.
